title: IBPS PO — English Language | Articles
description: Subject-wise test on Articles (English Language) for IBPS PO. 30Q.
subject: bank-english

questions.question: The sun rises in east. Identify the part with an error.

options.explanation: There is an error in the sentence

questions.explanation: The definite article 'the' must be used before geographical directions when they refer to a specific region or are preceded by a preposition.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: The science has made great strides in the last century. Identify the part with an error.
questions.explanation: When 'science' is used in a general sense, referring to the field of study, no article is required.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: The honesty is the best policy that one can adopt. Identify the part with an error.
questions.explanation: Abstract nouns like 'honesty' generally do not take an article when used in a general sense.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: Fill in the blanks: _____ sun rose over _____ Himalayas, painting _____ sky in hues of orange and pink.
questions.explanation: 'The' is used before unique celestial bodies like 'sun' and 'sky'. It is also used before names of mountain ranges, such as 'Himalayas'.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: Select the best option to replace the underlined part of the sentence: He is *an European* by birth, but has lived in Asia for most of his life.
questions.explanation: The choice between 'a' and 'an' depends on the sound of the word following the article.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: Find out which part of the sentence has an error: He eats a lunch at noon every day.
questions.explanation: Meals generally do not take an article when used in a general sense.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: Select the best option to replace the underlined part of the sentence: Although he had *few* friends, he was never lonely.
questions.explanation: 'Few' means 'hardly any' or 'almost none'. 'A few' means 'some, but not many'.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: Find out which part of the sentence has an error: The more you read, better you understand.
questions.explanation: In the comparative structure, 'the' is required before both comparative adjectives.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: Choose the most appropriate pair of words to fill in the blanks: Despite being _____ rich man, he lacked _____ wisdom, which is far more valuable than _____ wealth.
questions.explanation: The correct pair of words to fill in the blanks is 'a / a / a'.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: The manager of the bank insisted that Mr. Sharma was a honest man and should be promoted immediately.

options.text: a honest man and should be
options.explanation: The error is in this part. It should be 'an honest man'.

questions.explanation: The error is in part (C). The word 'honest' begins with a consonant 'h' but is pronounced with a vowel sound (like 'o' in 'orange'). Therefore, the indefinite article 'an' should be used instead of 'a'. It should be 'an honest man'.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: Despite being ______ avid reader, she found ______ latest novel by her favorite author quite challenging to finish.
questions.explanation: For the first blank, 'avid' starts with a vowel sound, so 'an' is required. For the second blank, 'latest' is a superlative adjective, which always takes the definite article 'the'. Thus, 'an avid reader' and 'the latest novel' are correct.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: He always believed that hard work is the key to a success in any field.

options.text: hard work is a key to the success
hard work is key to success
hard work is the key to success

questions.explanation: The phrase 'the key to success' is an idiomatic expression. 'Success' in this general context is an uncountable abstract noun and does not require an article. 'The key' is definite because it refers to *the* specific key (the means) to achieving success.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: Many people believe that the honesty is the best policy, but few truly practice it.

options.explanation: The error is in this part. It should be 'honesty is'.

options.text: the best policy, but few truly practice it

questions.explanation: The error is in part (B). 'Honesty' is an abstract noun used in a general sense, and abstract nouns generally do not take a definite article when spoken of generally. It should simply be 'honesty is the best policy'.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: He decided to pursue ______ career in medicine, hoping to make ______ difference in people's lives.
questions.explanation: For the first blank, 'career' is a singular countable noun, requiring the indefinite article 'a'. For the second blank, 'make a difference' is a common idiomatic phrase, where 'a' is always used.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: The Mount Everest is the highest peak in the world and attracts many climbers.

options.explanation: The error is in this part. It should be 'Mount Everest is'.

options.text: the highest peak in the world and attracts many climbers

questions.explanation: The error is in part (A). Proper nouns for single mountains (like Mount Everest, Mount Fuji, Mount Kilimanjaro) do not take the definite article 'the'. However, mountain ranges (e.g., The Himalayas, The Alps) do.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: It is generally accepted that the knowledge is the power in today's information age.
questions.explanation: 'Knowledge' and 'power' are abstract nouns used in a general sense in this proverb-like statement. Abstract nouns, when used generally, do not take articles. Therefore, both 'the' before 'knowledge' and 'the' before 'power' are incorrect.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: After a long and arduous journey, the team finally reached a summit of the mountain, feeling a sense of immense relief.

options.text: After a long and arduous journey, the team finally reached

options.explanation: The error is in this part. It should be 'the summit of the mountain'.

options.text: feeling a sense of immense relief

questions.explanation: The error is in part (C). It should be 'the summit of the mountain' or simply 'the summit' if the mountain is previously specified, but 'a summit' is incorrect because it implies any summit, not the specific one they were aiming for.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: Find out which part of the sentence has an error and mark it as your answer. If there is no error, mark 'D'. Despite being a honest man, he found it difficult to secure a loan.

options.explanation: The article 'a' is incorrect before 'honest' as it starts with a vowel sound.
There is an error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: The error is in part (A). The word 'honest' begins with a vowel sound (/ɒnɪst/), so the indefinite article 'an' should be used instead of 'a'. The correct phrase should be 'an honest man'.
questions.hint: Consider the sound of the word following the article.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: Choose the most appropriate article to complete the sentence. She is one of _____ few people who truly understand _____ importance of environmental conservation.

options.explanation: 'a' is incorrect for the first blank as 'one of the few' is the correct idiom.
'an' is incorrect for the second blank as 'importance' is used in a specific context.
Both blanks require 'the' for correct usage.
Both articles are incorrect for their respective blanks.

questions.explanation: The phrase 'one of the few' is a common idiom meaning a small number out of a larger group. 'Importance' is an abstract noun used in a specific context here, thus requiring 'the'.
questions.hint: Consider the idiomatic usage and the context of the abstract noun.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, choose option (D). The principal announced that a school would remain closed for a week due to heavy rains.

options.explanation: The article 'a' is incorrect as the school is specific.

options.text: for a week due to heavy rains.

options.explanation: There is an error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: The error is in part (B). When referring to a specific school already known to the speaker/listener (implied by 'The principal announced'), the definite article 'the' should be used, not 'a'. It should be 'the school would remain closed'.
questions.hint: Consider whether the noun is specific or general in context.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: Select the option that best replaces the underlined part of the sentence. If no improvement is needed, select (D). He has a great experience in the field of marketing and sales.

options.explanation: The article 'a' is incorrect before 'great experience' as it is an uncountable noun.
Both 'an' and 'a' are incorrect before 'great experience'.
The definite article 'the' is incorrect as 'experience' is used in a general sense.

questions.explanation: The error is in the underlined part. 'Experience' in the sense of knowledge or skill gained over time is an uncountable noun and generally does not take an indefinite article ('a' or 'an') when used in a general sense. Therefore, 'a great experience' should be corrected to 'great experience'.
questions.hint: Consider whether 'experience' is countable or uncountable in this context.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: Find out which part of the sentence has an error and mark it as your answer. If there is no error, mark 'D'. He went to hospital to visit his ailing friend, who had been admitted last night.

options.explanation: The article 'the' is missing before 'hospital' as it refers to a specific place.

options.text: who had been admitted last night.

options.explanation: There is an error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: The error is in part (A). When 'hospital' is referred to as a specific building or place where someone goes (not necessarily for treatment as a patient, but as a visitor), it requires the definite article 'the'. One goes 'to the hospital' to visit someone.
questions.hint: Consider whether the noun is being used in a general or specific sense.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: Choose the pair of words that best completes the sentence. It was _____ unusually warm day for December, and _____ children were enjoying themselves in the park.

options.explanation: 'a' is incorrect for the first blank as 'unusually' starts with a vowel sound.
Both articles are correct for their respective blanks.
'the' is incorrect for the first blank and 'a' is incorrect for the second blank.
'a' is incorrect for the second blank as the children are specific.

questions.explanation: The first blank requires 'an' because 'unusually' starts with a vowel sound (/ʌ/). The second blank refers to specific children (those enjoying themselves in the park), hence requiring the definite article 'the'.
questions.hint: Consider the sound of the word following the article and whether the noun is specific or general.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, choose option (D). The honesty is the best policy, a principle that guides many.

options.explanation: The definite article 'the' is incorrect before 'honesty' as it is used in a general sense.
There is an error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: The error is in part (A). 'Honesty' is an abstract noun used in a general sense. Abstract nouns in a general sense do not take the definite article 'the'. It should simply be 'Honesty is the best policy'.
questions.hint: Consider whether the abstract noun is being used in a general or specific sense.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: Select the option that best replaces the underlined part of the sentence. If no improvement is needed, select (D). He has little patience for those who do not understand the urgency of the matter.

options.explanation: 'a little patience' would mean 'some patience,' altering the intended meaning.
'the little patience' is grammatically incorrect in this context.
The original sentence is grammatically correct.

questions.explanation: The original sentence is correct. 'Little patience' (without 'a') means 'hardly any patience' or 'almost no patience,' which fits the context of someone being intolerant towards others' lack of understanding. 'A little patience' would mean 'some patience' or 'a small amount of patience,' which would alter the meaning.
questions.hint: Consider the nuanced difference between 'little' and 'a little'.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: Find out which part of the sentence has an error and mark it as your answer. If there is no error, mark 'D'. It is generally believed that the rich exploit the poor.
questions.explanation: This sentence is grammatically correct. 'The rich' and 'the poor' are correct uses of the definite article 'the' followed by an adjective to refer to a class or group of people (e.g., rich people, poor people).
questions.hint: Consider the specific rule for using 'the' with adjectives referring to groups of people.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, choose option (D). He considers himself a great philosopher, but in reality, he is a man of few words.

options.text: but in reality, he is a man of few words.
options.explanation: The phrase should be 'a man of a few words'.
There is an error in the sentence.

questions.explanation: The error is in part (C). The idiomatic phrase is 'a man of a few words,' meaning someone who does not speak much. 'Few words' without 'a' would imply almost no words, which changes the nuance of the idiom.
questions.hint: Consider the correct idiomatic usage of the phrase.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: The manager’s decision to promote Mr. Sharma was based on ___ consistent performance over ___ past five years.

options.explanation: Incorrect: 'a' is used for general nouns, but 'performance' here is specific.
Correct: Both blanks require definite articles for specificity.
Incorrect: 'an' is for vowel sounds, but 'performance' starts with a consonant sound.
Incorrect: The second blank requires 'the' for a defined period.

questions.explanation: The first blank requires the definite article 'the' because 'performance' is being specified as the manager's particular performance. The second blank needs 'the' because 'past five years' refers to a specific, defined period of time.
questions.hint: Consider whether the noun is specific or general and whether it refers to a unique or defined period.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: After ___ hour-long meeting with ___ union leaders, the CEO announced ___ new policy that would benefit all employees.

options.explanation: Incorrect: The third blank requires 'the' for a specific policy.
Incorrect: 'Hour' starts with a vowel sound, so 'an' is needed.
Correct: All blanks use the appropriate articles.
Incorrect: 'Union leaders' is a specific group, so 'the' is needed.

questions.explanation: 'Hour' starts with a vowel sound, so 'an' is correct for the first blank. 'Union leaders' is a specific group, so 'the' is needed. The third blank requires 'the' because the new policy is being specified as a particular policy.
questions.hint: Pay attention to vowel sounds for 'a' vs. 'an' and whether the noun is specific or general.
questions.subject: bank-english

questions.question: Despite living in ___ United States for over a decade, she still struggles with ___ use of definite and indefinite articles in her writing.

options.explanation: Correct: Both blanks use 'the' for specificity.
Incorrect: 'United States' is a proper noun and requires 'the'.
Incorrect: 'Use' here refers to a specific concept, so 'the' is needed.
Incorrect: 'United States' is a proper noun and requires 'the,' not 'an'.

questions.explanation: The first blank requires 'the' because 'United States' is a proper noun referring to a specific country. The second blank also requires 'the' because 'use' is a specific concept being referred to in general terms.
questions.hint: Proper nouns like countries typically use 'the,' and abstract nouns like 'use' may require 'the' when referring to a specific instance.
questions.subject: bank-english
